text:
Austin, the legal positivist, is called a naive empiricist because his command theory treats law as the observable command of a sovereign backed by threats, generalizing from a simple historical model of a legal system. That picture of a determinate sovereign habitually obeyed no longer fits modern constitutional, federal, and limited legal orders, so the description is anachronistic. Denying a necessary link between law and morality is his positivism, not what “naive empiricist” names.

CONFIDENCE: 78
